meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.

examples.text: Господи, как я вообще здесь оказался?
examples.trans: Good Lord, how on earth did I end up here?

examples.text: Мне вообще нельзя такие тяжести таскать!
examples.trans: I must not haul such heavy loads at all!

examples.text: Они в обычном магазине вообще не продаются!
examples.trans: They are not sold in an ordinary store at all!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему вы о ней раньше не говорили?
examples.trans: Why did you never speak about her before?

examples.text: Девушка, мы случайно утром вместе не просыпались?
examples.trans: Miss, did we not happen to wake up together this morning?

examples.text: Шеф, ну не расстраивайтесь вы так сильно!
examples.trans: Chef, well do not get so upset like that!

продаваться.gloss: to be sold; to sell oneself

meanings.en: to be sold; to sell oneself
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'даваться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be sold', forming an aspectual pair with 'продаться'.

examples.text: Они в обычном магазине вообще не продаются!
examples.trans: They are not sold in an ordinary store at all!

examples.text: Я не продаюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not for sale.

examples.text: Квартира продаётся.
examples.trans: The flat is for sale.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.text: Надо срочно ехать на другой конец Москвы.
examples.trans: One must urgently go to the other end of Moscow.

examples.text: Не надо придавать этому вечеру большого значения.
examples.trans: There is no need to attach great importance to this evening.

examples.text: Значит, нам надо тихо внедриться внутрь.
examples.trans: That means we need to quietly infiltrate inside.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'urgently'.

examples.text: Надо срочно ехать на другой конец Москвы.
examples.trans: One must urgently go to the other end of Moscow.

examples.text: А белые порошки срочно отправим на экспертизу!
examples.trans: And we will urgently send the white powders for testing!

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно!
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'поехать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Надо срочно ехать на другой конец Москвы.
examples.trans: One must urgently go to the other end of Moscow.

examples.text: Виталик, в Санта-Фе едем.
examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Через полчаса жду тебя на рабочем месте!
examples.trans: In half an hour I expect you at your workstation!

examples.text: Если опоздаешь на работу, я тебя оштрафую!
examples.trans: If you are late for work, I will fine you!

examples.text: Ой, я уже сильно опаздываю на работу!
examples.trans: Oh, I am already running very late for work!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'other', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Но вчера вечером ты говорила совсем другое!
examples.trans: But last night you were saying something completely different!

examples.text: У нынешней молодёжи сейчас совсем другие взгляды.
examples.trans: Today's youth have completely different views now.

examples.text: Надо срочно ехать на другой конец Москвы.
examples.trans: One must urgently go to the other end of Moscow.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'end', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Надо срочно ехать на другой конец Москвы.
examples.trans: One must urgently go to the other end of Moscow.

examples.text: Это конец.
examples.trans: This is the end.

examples.text: Конец связи.
examples.trans: Over and out.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'Moscow', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: В самом лучшем французском ресторане Москвы.
examples.trans: In the very best French restaurant in Moscow.

examples.text: Ресторан Клод Моне в Москве.
examples.trans: Restaurant Claude Monet in Moscow.

examples.text: Наш ресторан — один из лучших в Москве!
examples.trans: Our restaurant is one of the best in Moscow!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'necessary'.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить.
examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Тебе нужно отдохнуть.
examples.trans: You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (root 'третиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встречаться'.

examples.text: Нужно встретиться с поставщиком, а времени мало.
examples.trans: One needs to meet with the supplier, and there is little time.

examples.text: Может, встретимся сейчас?
examples.trans: Maybe we could meet now?

examples.text: Встретимся в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's meet in the café.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'with' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: У тебя со мной нет никаких шансов.
examples.trans: You have no chances with me at all.

examples.text: Смотри, это билет на свидание со мной.
examples.trans: Look, this is a ticket for a date with me.

examples.text: Нужно встретиться с поставщиком, а времени мало.
examples.trans: One needs to meet with the supplier, and there is little time.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'supplier', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Нужно встретиться с поставщиком, а времени мало.
examples.trans: One needs to meet with the supplier, and there is little time.

examples.text: А вот и серьёзные поставщики приехали сюда!
examples.trans: And here the serious suppliers have arrived here!

examples.text: Поставщик привезёт банку через час.
examples.trans: The supplier will bring the jar in an hour.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!
examples.trans: Yesterday the drink was speaking, and now the boss is speaking!

examples.text: А у меня на кухне строгий начальник!
examples.trans: And I have a strict boss in the kitchen!

examples.text: А это моя любимая племянница приехала!
examples.trans: Oh, this is my beloved niece who arrived!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Нужно встретиться с поставщиком, а времени мало.
examples.trans: One needs to meet with the supplier, and there is little time.

examples.text: Лёва, ты совсем не следишь за временем!
examples.trans: Lyova, you are not watching the time at all!

examples.text: У меня нет времени.
examples.trans: I don't have time.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'little'.

examples.text: Нужно встретиться с поставщиком, а времени мало.
examples.trans: One needs to meet with the supplier, and there is little time.

examples.text: Два дня — это мало.
examples.trans: Two days isn't enough.

examples.text: У нас мало времени.
examples.trans: We have little time.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('let's') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давай убирать!
examples.trans: Let's clean up!

examples.text: Давай, пока!
examples.trans: See you, bye!

examples.text: Аркаша, давай убирать!
examples.trans: Arkasha, let's clean up!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'fast'.

examples.text: Катя, давай я быстро съезжу за ними!
examples.trans: Katya, let me quickly make a round trip for them!

examples.text: Ничего, наша машина тебя сейчас быстро подвезёт!
examples.trans: No problem, our car will give you a quick ride right now!

examples.text: Меня на кухне попросили быстро это купить.
examples.trans: They asked me in the kitchen to buy this quickly.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'round', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Катя, давай я быстро съезжу за ними!
examples.trans: Katya, let me quickly make a round trip for them!

examples.text: Я ещё раз спрашиваю, где мои загустители?
examples.trans: I am asking once more, where are my thickeners?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Катя, давай я быстро съезжу за ними!
examples.trans: Katya, let me quickly make a round trip for them!

examples.text: Ого, а что это за белые пакеты?
examples.trans: Whoa, and what kind of white packets are these?

examples.text: Скажите, девушка, а что это за порошки?
examples.trans: Tell me, miss, what kind of powders are those?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'there'.

examples.text: Тебе туда плохое мясо положили.
examples.trans: They put bad meat in there for you.

examples.text: Пойдём туда вместе.
examples.trans: Let's go there together.

examples.text: Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: Want them to take you there too right now?
